answer: Randomness-gated identity slots. Each join attempt draws a public verifiable-randomness value; agents whose draw falls outside a narrow admission band are deferred to a future round, otherwise a kernel check binds the new ID to that round's seed. Attackers cannot know admission outcomes before committing resources, so mass pre-registration fails and they must wander across many rounds, paying full registration and re-draw costs per identity. Forced waiting also raises the ivory-tower cost of maintaining a synchronized bot farm, since each ID needs a live committed draw.
